$comment: The log of speed barriers broken. A row is added when a barrier actually falls, with the evidence that it fell; nothing goes in as a forecast. The 'then' figures are the ones docs/rapp-guide.html shipped with, kept deliberately so the gain is measurable rather than remembered. tests/test_speed_barriers.py checks that every entry here is also stated in the guide's Speed Barriers Broken section.

baseline.note: Every duration in the original guide was measured and was true when written. The barriers below record what changed underneath the method, not a correction of the method.

barriers.then: 2-3 weeks per agent, hand-written. Step 5 called it days to weeks and set the goal at hours.
barriers.now: Minutes. A scaffolded agent is generated, smoke-tested and hot-loaded in about fifteen seconds; a hand-written one is live the moment the file is saved.
barriers.caveat: The generated perform() is a scaffold. Writing the business logic inside it is still the real work.
barriers.evidence: The LearnNew agent ships in the Brainstem's default agent set; measured at 15.9s from description to hot-loaded agent.

barriers.then: 3-5 days: code change, testing, approval, deployment.
barriers.now: The next question, locally. The local server re-reads its agents folder on every request; the cloud tier refreshes on a five-minute cache.
barriers.evidence: Measured on a running install: a file saved at 10:27:45 answered on the very next request with no restart, and disappeared within a second of deletion.

barriers.barrier: Set up before you can learn anything
barriers.then: An Azure subscription, a Function App, a storage account, and a deployment before the first lesson.
barriers.now: One command. No cloud account, no subscription and no model key: the server borrows existing GitHub Copilot access.
barriers.evidence: install.sh; the auth chain resolves a Copilot token by device code and never asks for a provider API key.

barriers.then: Every engagement began with a blank transcript and an empty folder.
barriers.now: 52 published solutions, each a single-file agent with tested operations, a guided workshop and a Copilot Studio solution beside it.
barriers.evidence: registry.json: 72 agents, 52 stacks, 30,699 lines; 51 complete workshops under solutions/.

barriers.barrier: Put a demo in front of the field
barriers.then: Planned as a shared, non-expiring cloud tenant with live endpoints so nobody had to deploy per demo.
barriers.now: No shared tenant at all. The catalog and its workshops are public, and any agent is one command away on a laptop.
barriers.evidence: The 2025 plan's third priority, versus the published catalog and the one-liner installer.

barriers.barrier: Hand a prototype to Copilot Studio
barriers.then: Built by hand in the portal, per agent.
barriers.now: A Copilot Studio solution and its deployment settings ship beside every published workshop, 51 of them today.

barriers.barrier: Described use case to working prototype
barriers.now: Minutes, when the library already covers the problem.
barriers.caveat: Production deployment is still 3-5 weeks, and still mostly waiting for security and compliance.
barriers.evidence: Step 14 of the original guide, versus a measured clean install.

still_standing.note: This is the longest pole in the guide and no tooling has moved it. It is a review by people who are right to take their time.
The 2025 plan wanted speech-to-text timing so demos assembled themselves. It did not ship.
Scaffolding an agent is now seconds. Knowing what the agent should actually do is still the work.
